tool_signatures.name: addAgentModel
tool_signatures.description:
Add an avatar model to an agent you already created — no need to
re-create the agent or regenerate its persona/voice/image. The agent
must be in the `ready` state (else `409 AGENT_NOT_READY`).

| model | what happens | prerequisites | credits | time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `expression-1` | **immediate enablement** — the v1 engine drives the agent's existing image + voice at runtime; nothing is trained | stored image + voice + real-human subject (else `422 MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH`) | **0** | immediate (this response) |
| `expression-2` | trains the per-identity Expression 2 model from the stored image | stored image | 2000 | the same training an `expression-2` creation runs — about 2–2.5 h (see [creation times](#operation/generateAgent)) |
| `essence-2` | trains Essence 2 from the agent's stored identity video (generated internally at creation) | stored identity video (else `422`) + photorealistic-human subject (else `422 MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH`) | 500 | the same training an `essence-2` creation runs — about 2–2.5 h (see [creation times](#operation/generateAgent)) |
| `essence-1` | builds the v1 `.imx` from the agent's stored identity video (or generates one internally from the stored image) | stored identity video or image + real-human subject (else `422 MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH`) | 250 | ~10–20 min |

Asynchronous adds return `status: "processing"` — poll
[`GET /v1/agent/status/{agent_id}`](#tag/Agent-Generation/operation/getAgentStatus)
until `supported_models` contains the new family. Charges are refunded
automatically if the add fails; re-POSTing the same model never
double-charges, and returns `status: "ready"` with `credits: 0` once
the model already exists.

model.description: The model to add. Anything else returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` listing these options.

tool_signatures.name: downloadAgentModel
tool_signatures.description:
Download the generated model file for an agent you own. The family
defaults to the agent's own model; override with `?model=<family>`
(canonical names, legacy names, and runtime tier slugs all fold onto
their family). Artifact per family:

| family | artifact |
|---|---|
| `essence-1` | `<code>.imx` (the portable IMX container) |
| `essence-2` | `<CODE>.imx` — the standard Essence 2 artifact (unified IMX container; size is per identity — read `Content-Length` rather than assuming a figure; **licensed weights** — renders locally in the CLI, the Python SDK, the Android library and the Swift `Essence2` product, and the first local play checks the license with the cloud, so it needs a sign-in: https://docs.bithuman.ai/platforms/cli/voice#platform-notes). |
| `expression-2` | `<code>.avatar` — the same container as `.imx` under a second name (a few early identities use an older format; `bithuman open` reports which) — runs locally on macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux x86_64, or in the browser, and is also served on bitHuman's cloud |
| `expression-1` | normally not downloadable (the shared v1 engine renders server-side from the agent's image) → `400 MODEL_NOT_DOWNLOADABLE`; an agent that went through the lip step owns a baked `<code>.imx` and is redirected to it like `essence-1` |

The default response is a **302 redirect** to the artifact — the
public URL for `essence-1`, a **1-hour signed URL** on a private
bucket for the other families — so `curl -L` and browser anchors just
work. Pass `?redirect=false` to get the URL as JSON instead.

**Name the file yourself** (`curl -L -o "<CODE>.imx"`). The redirect
target does not always send a `Content-Disposition` header — the
public `essence-1` URL sends none — so a filename-from-the-header
flag such as `curl -LOJ` silently falls back to the last path segment
of the request URL and writes a file called `download`. With
`?redirect=false` the JSON carries the intended name in `filename`.

The launchability gate doubles as the download gate: a family the
agent can't be launched as (missing from `supported_models`) returns
`409 MODEL_NOT_GENERATED`. A family the agent supports whose artifact
hasn't been published to the download store yet returns
`404 MODEL_ARTIFACT_NOT_READY` — the message says when to retry;
**poll on that code**.

**Every grant is recorded.** A model download costs **0 credits** on
the [pricing table](https://docs.bithuman.ai/pricing) — only
runtime minutes bill — but the grant still writes exactly one usage row
before the URL is issued, under the family's self-hosted pricing code,
and hands you its id in `X-Bithuman-Meter-Id`. The rows show up in
`GET /v1/usage` at 0 credits; they are a record of what you fetched,
not a charge. The order matters both ways: a meter that refuses
(`402`) or fails (`500`) returns no URL at all.

The [bitHuman CLI](https://docs.bithuman.ai/platforms/cli/reference) wraps
this endpoint: `bithuman pull <AGENT_CODE>` downloads the artifact,
recognizes its model family, and prints what to do next.

**Showcase identities need no credential.** The `essence-2` and
`expression-2` identities listed by
[`GET /v1/models/showcase`](#tag/Agent-Management/operation/getShowcaseManifest)
are served to anonymous callers — same 302, same 1-hour signed URL, and
the owner is charged **0 credits**. Every other agent still needs the
`api-secret` header (or `Authorization: Bearer <api-secret | runtime
token>`) and must be owned by the caller; an anonymous request for one
answers `401 MISSING_AUTH`, the same answer an unknown code gets.

code.description: Agent code. The agent must be owned by the caller (else 404) — except for the showcase identities in `GET /v1/models/showcase`, which are served with no credential.

model.description: Artifact family. Defaults to the agent's own model. The runtime tier slugs (`essence-2-apple`, `essence-2-gpu`, `essence-2-cpu`, `expression-2-gpu`; the older `essence-2-ane` spelling stays accepted) fold onto their family. `essence-2-quality` returns `400`; send `essence-2`. Any other unrecognized value returns the same `400`, listing the downloadable families.

member.description: Fetch ONE on-device model member instead of the whole container. `essence-2` and `expression-2` publish a browser/Android bundle beside the container — a `web_manifest.json` and the members it lists (`combined_fp32.tflite`, `canon.bin`, ...) — and this serves a single one of them, so a browser or an Android runtime pulls only the files it runs. Same entitlement as the container, same 1-hour signed URL, and the URL honours `Range` (`curl -L -r 0-1023` answers `206`, so OkHttp and browsers resume). Pass `web_manifest.json` first to learn the member names. A member of a **public** agent is served to an anonymous caller, like the browser already serves those agents; every other visibility needs the same credential as the container.

plane.description: Which member set `?member=` names. `essence-2` publishes two — one for browsers and one for Android — and twelve names appear in both of them, `manifest.json` among them. A browser asking for `manifest.json` and a handset asking for `manifest.json` want different files, so for those twelve the request has to say which set it means. Only meaningful alongside `member=`: the container itself has one form, so `plane=` on its own returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, as does any value not listed above. **You can usually leave it out.** A member that appears in only one of the two sets identifies itself — which is why the Android runtime's first call, `member=android_store.v1.json`, resolves with no `plane=` at all. When a name appears in both and the request says nothing, it resolves to the browser set, so every caller written before this parameter behaves exactly as it did.

redirect.description: Pass `false` to receive the artifact URL as JSON (below) instead of a 302 redirect — for UIs that want to fetch or label first.

tool_signatures.name: generateAgent
tool_signatures.description:
Create a new avatar agent from a text prompt, with optional image
and audio assets. Poll `/v1/agent/status/{agent_id}` to check
progress.

**Agent creation is image-only.** Provide a portrait `image` (or let
the prompt generate one) — bitHuman generates a **10-second
identity video internally**, authored to loop without a seam (its
first and last frames match). A `video` field is rejected with
`400 VIDEO_INPUT_NOT_SUPPORTED` before anything is billed.

**Selecting a model.** Always send `model`: `essence-2`,
`expression-2`, `auto`, `essence-1` or `expression-1`. An omitted
`model` creates an `expression-1` agent. A model outside your plan
returns `403 PLAN_REQUIRED`.

**Creation time depends on the model** (the second-generation models
train a per-identity model, so don't apply a 5-minute client
timeout):

| `model` | identity input | creation time |
|---|---|---|
| `essence-2` | image (or generated from prompt); a 10-second identity video is generated internally | about 2–2.5 h |
| `expression-2` | image (or generated from prompt) | about 2–2.5 h |
| `auto` | image or prompt (classified automatically) | as the routed model (`essence-2` or `expression-2`) |
| `essence-1` | image (or generated from prompt) | under 15 min |
| `expression-1` (the default when `model` is omitted) | image (or generated from prompt) | about 1 min |

Times run from this call to `status: "ready"` on
`GET /v1/agent/status/{agent_id}`. They are a typical range, not a
guarantee, and individual runs can take longer: size timeouts in
hours for the second-generation models.

**Picking the right family** ([Choosing a model](https://docs.bithuman.ai/models#choosing-a-model)):
`essence-2` for a real person; `expression-2` for a cartoon,
stylized, animal, creature or robot character. Send
`model: "auto"` to apply this rule automatically — the platform
classifies your input and records the recommended model either way.

**Subject requirement:** every model except `expression-2` needs a
clear, **real human face**: `essence-2`, `essence-1` and
`expression-1` (also when `model` is omitted). The input is
classified before anything is billed; a cartoon, stylized
character, animal, creature or robot, or a photo with no face
found, is rejected with `422 MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH` (nothing
charged) — use `expression-2` for those characters, or send
`model: "auto"` to route automatically.

Failures during generation surface as `status: "failed"` with an
`error_message` on the status endpoint, and the creation credits
are automatically refunded.

Idempotency-Key.description: Optional. A unique client-generated key (e.g. a UUID). Retrying with the same key returns the original response instead of starting a second billed job. Keys are retained for 24 hours.

prompt.description: System prompt / personality for the agent. If omitted, a random default is used.
prompt.example: You are a friendly fitness coach who motivates users.

image.description: URL to a face image for avatar appearance. For the best likeness use a photo with one clear figure, a neutral expression, facing the camera, a relaxed pose, and no occlusion of the face. Every model except Expression 2 needs a real human face (otherwise 422 `MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH`), and Essence 2 needs the face clearly in frame (otherwise 422 `IMAGE_FACE_UNSUITABLE`), before any charge.

audio.description: URL to audio for voice cloning.

aspect_ratio.description: Aspect ratio for the generated identity image and driver video. `16:9` landscape (default), `9:16` portrait, `1:1` square. Images are generated at 1080p on this ratio.

transparency.description: When `true`, the identity image is generated on a solid green-screen background (chroma-key friendly) so the avatar can be embedded transparently — the character itself never uses green. Leave `false` for a normal scene background.

framing.description: `portrait` (default) frames head-and-shoulders; `full_body` shows the full figure including the feet — use it for kiosk / standing-avatar layouts.

agent_id.description: Custom agent identifier. Auto-generated if omitted.

duration.description: **Deprecated — omit it.** The internally generated identity video is 10 seconds (authored to loop without a seam); this parameter is ignored.

model.description:
Which model to create. Always send it; if omitted, an `expression-1` agent is created (250 credits). A model outside your plan returns `403 PLAN_REQUIRED`. The bare family names `essence` and `expression` are still accepted for older integrations (they select the version-1 model); new code should send a full model name.

**`essence-2`** is the second-generation Essence model for photorealistic people — one 500-credit creation that runs everywhere from on-device (CPU / Apple Silicon) up to cloud GPU. **`expression-2`** is the second-generation expression engine — audio-driven real-time avatar video from a single photo (creation trains a per-identity model — about 2 hours, as does `essence-2`; see the creation-time table above). **`auto`** classifies your input (the image if provided, else the prompt): a photorealistic person routes to `essence-2`, a cartoon / animal / creature / robot to `expression-2`. Retired engine names return `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. Identity inputs and creation times differ per model — see the endpoint description table and [Compare models](https://docs.bithuman.ai/models).

version.description: **Older form — send a full model name in `model` instead.** With a bare family name in `model` (`essence` or `expression`), `v1` selects the first-generation model and `v2` the second-generation one. Ignored when `model` is a full model name or `auto`.

tool_signatures.name: generateTalkingVideo
tool_signatures.description:
Render a talking-video (mp4) from **your audio**, driven by one of
your agents.

**Two modes:**
- **Async (default)** — returns immediately with a `job_id`; poll
  [`GET /v1/video/{job_id}`](#operation/getTalkingVideo) for the finished
  video. Use this for anything but the shortest clips — renders can take a
  while, so you don't want to hold the connection.
- **Sync** — set `wait: true` (or `?wait=true`). The call blocks until the
  render finishes (up to ~90s) and returns the `video_url` directly in this
  response. If the render is still running at that cap you get the async
  response (`status: processing`) instead — just poll the `job_id`.

**Input:** your own audio. `audio_url` (a hosted WAV/MP3: a recording, or
the output of any text-to-speech tool) drives the render directly.

The output is a public CDN URL. `essence-2` renders at
**1080p** by default (1080×1920 portrait or 1920×1080 landscape, matching
the source orientation and capped at the source's long side);
`expression-2` renders at its native 416×720. Limits: max **120 seconds**
of output.

Idempotency-Key.description: Optional. A unique client-generated key (e.g. a UUID). Retrying with the same key returns the original response instead of starting a second billed job. Keys are retained for 24 hours.

model.description:
Avatar engine. `essence-1` (2 credits/min) and
`expression-1` (4 credits/min) are the classic v1 engines,
available today. `expression-2` (4 credits/min) and `essence-2`
(4 credits/min) are the v2 engines.

agent_code.description: An agent you own, or a public sample from `GET /v1/models/showcase` (audio input, a model in its `supported_models`) — provides the avatar identity.

wait.description: Sync toggle. `false` (default) returns a `job_id` immediately (async — poll for the result). `true` blocks until the render finishes (up to ~90s) and returns the finished `video_url` in this response; if it exceeds the cap you get `status: processing` + a `job_id` to poll. `?wait=true` as a query parameter also works.

audio_url.description: A public URL to a WAV or MP3 file.

tool_signatures.name: getAgentStatus
tool_signatures.description:
Poll this endpoint to check generation progress. Status values:
`processing`, `generating`, `completed`, `success` (all intermediate);
`ready` (terminal success); `failed` (terminal error).

**Keep polling past `generating`, `completed` and `success`** — those
are intermediate states, not terminal. `completed` can appear early
(even around ~5% `progress`), and `success` is a STEP-level marker the
voice/image and video steps each write (~20% and ~45% `progress`), so
do not stop on either. Only `ready` and `failed` mean polling should
stop — or `success` when `progress` has also reached `1.0`.

`current_step` reports the pipeline stage: `payment` (~2%) →
`persona` (5–15%) → `voice_image` (~20%) → `video` (~45%, the
internally generated 10-second identity video — models that need
one) → `lip_sync` (70–99%, the
model-specific identity step — training/distillation for
`expression-2` / `essence-2`, so the longest stage) → `done`
(100%). A rare `essence-1` path reports `awaiting_face_marking`
(~35%).

Recommended polling interval: 5 seconds. Size your overall timeout to
the model: minutes for the first-generation engines, **hours** for
both second-generation ones (about 2–2.5 hours from creation to `ready`).

**`ready` does not yet mean downloadable.** The agent can be launched
and embedded as soon as it reports `ready`, but the downloadable
model file is published separately, shortly afterwards. Until it is,
`GET /v1/agent/{code}/model/download` answers
`404 MODEL_ARTIFACT_NOT_READY` — a retryable code, not a failure. It
can take a few minutes after `ready`; poll the download while it
answers `404 MODEL_ARTIFACT_NOT_READY`.

tool_signatures.name: getCloudAvatarSession
tool_signatures.description:
A [cloud avatar](https://docs.bithuman.ai/platforms/livekit/cloud-avatar)
session you started: `status` (`starting`, `live` or `ended`), times,
`billed_seconds` and `credits` so far.

tool_signatures.name: getCreditSummaries
tool_signatures.description:
Returns the current credit balance, plan details, and estimated minutes
remaining for each usage type. Always scoped to the **authenticated
account** (the owner of the `api-secret`) — there is no way to look up
another user.

tool_signatures.name: getDynamics
tool_signatures.description: List all available gesture animations for an agent.

tool_signatures.name: getMe
tool_signatures.description: The canonical account preflight — returns your identity, plan, and live credit balance in one call. Use it to show "who am I / how many credits" and to gate features before a billable call.

tool_signatures.name: getPricing
tool_signatures.description: Machine-readable credit pricing for billable operations, so you can estimate cost before a call. Authoritative charges are always enforced server-side at request time. For forward per-minute realtime estimates based on your current balance, see `GET /v2/credit-summaries` (`minutes_estimate`).

tool_signatures.name: getProviders
tool_signatures.description:
Your configured provider keys (BYOK). Sensitive keys are returned only
as `{present, hint, updated_at}`, never in full.

tool_signatures.name: getReadiness
tool_signatures.description:
Whether the API is refusing work right now. No credential required.
It always answers HTTP 200: read the `status` field (`ok`, `degraded`
or `unhealthy`). For the overall service status, use
[status.bithuman.ai](https://status.bithuman.ai).

tool_signatures.name: getRuntimeSessionMessages
tool_signatures.description:
The conversation, oldest first. Only cloud voice and chat sessions
record a transcript; self-hosted sessions return `messages: []`.

tool_signatures.name: getShowcaseManifest
tool_signatures.description:
The catalogue of **Essence 2** and **Expression 2** showcase identities
whose model weights anyone may download — no api-secret, no account.

Each entry's `url` is
[`GET /v1/agent/{code}/model/download`](#tag/Agent-Management/operation/downloadAgentModel),
which answers a **302** to a 1-hour signed URL for anonymous callers
too. The grant is still recorded (one usage row) and costs the agent's
owner **0 credits** — an anonymous download is free or refused, never
billed to the owner.

The list is generated from the download route's own admission
predicate, so a code listed here is a code the route serves: an
`essence-2` or `expression-2` identity that is ready, listed in the
agent gallery, owns its own artifact, and whose owner has authorised
anonymous distribution of the weights. Agents that are merely public in
the gallery are **not** here — being viewable is a different permission
from the weights being distributable.

The shape is the bitHuman CLI's manifest v2; `bithuman list` and
`bithuman pull` read this catalogue.

**Performance.** The reply carries no frame rates.
`note_performance` maps each family in the catalogue to the
[performance page](https://docs.bithuman.ai/performance), where the frame rates are
measured and published for every device.

`sha256` is deliberately empty: no content digest is recorded for these
objects yet, and the CLI skips verification on an empty value rather
than failing. Verify `size` and the file itself (`bithuman open`)
instead.

Throttled per IP; the reply is cached for 60 seconds.

tool_signatures.name: getTalkingVideo
tool_signatures.description:
Poll a talking-video render job. While rendering, `status` is `processing`.
When done, `status` is `completed` and the response carries `video_url`,
`duration_seconds`, and `credits_charged`. On failure, `status` is `failed`
and the up-front charge is automatically refunded.

tool_signatures.name: getUsage

Return your account's usage / activity history, newest first. Each row
is a metered event. `credits_change` is the signed credit delta — usage
events are recorded as **positive** credits consumed.

tool_signatures.name: listAgentSessions
tool_signatures.description:
The sessions this agent has open now. Pass a returned `room_id` to
/speak or /add-context to address ONE session instead of broadcasting.
`deliverable` is false when the room is live but no agent worker is
attached — /speak on such a room returns 404.

tool_signatures.name: listAgents
tool_signatures.description:
List the agents owned by your API secret, newest first. Paginated.

Each item is a **summary**, not the full agent record: it carries the
identity, the state and the launch surface, and nothing else. The
prompt, the progress fields, the media URLs and the model handle are
only on [`GET /v1/agent/{code}`](#operation/getAgent) — a caller that
reads them from a list item reads fields that are not there.

**Deleted agents are not listed and not counted.** Every page holds
`limit` items except the last. `pagination.total` is the number of
agents you reach by paging, and it is the same on every page. Pass
`?status=ready` if you want only agents that finished generating.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (1–100).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of agents to skip.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by generation state (e.g. `ready`, `processing`, `failed`).

tool_signatures.name: listApiSecrets
tool_signatures.description:
Your API secrets, masked. The raw secret is never returned here, only
`key_display`. `name`, `key` and `alias` all carry the alias label.

tool_signatures.name: listKnowledgeBases
tool_signatures.description: The organization's knowledge bases, newest first, each with `agent_count` and `source_count`.

tool_signatures.name: listRuntimeSessions
tool_signatures.description:
Your sessions plus live account KPIs (`active_count`,
`live_burn_rate_cr_per_min`, `credits_this_hour`, account-wide over the
last hour). A transient `500 UPSTREAM_ERROR` can be retried.

parameters.description: `conversations` (cloud), `self_hosted`, or `all`.

parameters.name: limit

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: `live` (only running), `recent` (idle + ended), or `all`.

tool_signatures.name: listWebhooks

tool_signatures.name: mintScopedRuntimeToken
tool_signatures.description:
Exchange your API secret, **server-side**, for a 1-hour token bound to a
single `agent_code` — so a browser, a phone app or any other client you
do not fully control never holds your master secret.

This is the credential the on-device paths accept. It works as
`Authorization: Bearer <scoped_token>` on
[the model download route](#operation/downloadAgentModel), including
the `?member=` fetch the browser and Android runtimes use.

The scope is real: presenting the token for a **different** agent code
answers `404`, exactly like a code you do not own. It expires in one
hour and is not refreshable — mint another.

**LiveKit plugin.** With `"scope": "livekit-cloud"` this mints the token
to pass to `livekit-plugins-bithuman` as `api_secret` instead of your API
secret. The plugin writes that value into LiveKit room attributes, where
every participant can read it. This token can only start this agent's
cloud avatar session. It is also bound to `room_name` and `livekit_url`
when you send them, and it bills your account. For another agent, room
or LiveKit server it answers `403`. It cannot download the model or call
any other endpoint. See [LiveKit integration](/platforms/livekit).

Call this from your server. Never ship the api-secret this endpoint
consumes to a client.

agent_code.description: The one agent this token may act for.

scope.description: `livekit-cloud` mints the launch-only token for the LiveKit plugin's cloud mode. Omit it for the runtime token described above.

room_name.description: `livekit-cloud` only. Binds the token to this LiveKit room.

livekit_url.description: `livekit-cloud` only. Binds the token to this LiveKit server. It must be the URL the plugin connects to.

parameters.name: agent_code
parameters.description: The one agent this token may act for.

parameters.name: livekit_url
parameters.description: `livekit-cloud` only. Binds the token to this LiveKit server. It must be the URL the plugin connects to.

parameters.name: room_name
parameters.description: `livekit-cloud` only. Binds the token to this LiveKit room.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `livekit-cloud` mints the launch-only token for the LiveKit plugin's cloud mode. Omit it for the runtime token described above.

tool_signatures.name: postMeterBeat
tool_signatures.description:
The bitHuman SDKs, the CLI and the plugins call this for you: a
self-hosted or on-device session reports its running time here, and
that is what bills it ([Pricing](https://docs.bithuman.ai/pricing)).
You call it only if you build your own runtime.

A report covers the seconds the session ran, idle included, not frames
rendered. The product (`billing_type`) is fixed by the first report of a
session.

Read **only the status code**:

| status | meaning | what a runtime should do |
|---|---|---|
| `2xx` | the interval is recorded | count it as reported |
| `402` | balance depleted / account suspended | **keep rendering**, report it again later |
| `401` | definite bad key | stop |
| `503` | we cannot tell right now | retry |

A `402` never stops a running session; the next session is refused
until you top up. A retried report (same `session_id`, `install_id`
and `seq`) is never charged twice.

session_id.description: Stable id for the session being billed.

seq.description: Beat sequence number within the session.

served_s.description:
Seconds of session covered by this beat. Clamped
server-side; wall-clock, idle included.

billing_type.description:
The self-hosted product wire key. Always send the key
for the product you run.

parameters.name: billing_type
parameters.description:
The self-hosted product wire key. Always send the key
for the product you run.

parameters.name: install_id
parameters.description: Stable id for this installation.

parameters.name: seq
parameters.description: Beat sequence number within the session.

parameters.name: served_s
parameters.description:
Seconds of session covered by this beat. Clamped
server-side; wall-clock, idle included.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: Stable id for the session being billed.

tool_signatures.name: realtimeConnect
tool_signatures.description:
Starts a WebRTC voice call: send the SDP offer as the body
(`Content-Type: application/sdp`) with `?model=gpt-realtime-mini`; a
`201` carries the SDP answer, and the `X-Bithuman-Call` header names
the call. End it with a JSON body `{"action": "hangup", "call": …}` —
billing stops when you hang up. See
[Realtime](https://docs.bithuman.ai/api/realtime#webrtc).

model.description: The Realtime model, fixed for the call.

parameters.name: call
parameters.description: The `X-Bithuman-Call` value from the start.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The Realtime model, fixed for the call.

tool_signatures.name: rebuildKnowledgeBase
tool_signatures.description:
Re-indexes a knowledge base after its sources change. Returns the
queued build row; indexing runs in the background. Builds run one at a
time per account, up to 20 per day.

tool_signatures.name: requestEmbedToken
tool_signatures.description: Generate a JWT token for embedding an avatar on a website. Use this from your backend — never expose your API secret in frontend code.

fingerprint.description: Stable per-device hex string used for session tracking and per-visitor rate limiting. Required.

model.description: Optional. Request a specific avatar model for the embed session — a model name (`essence-1`, `expression-1`, `essence-2`, `expression-2`) or a force-tier slug that pins one serving tier (`expression-2-gpu/-cpu/-apple`, `essence-2-gpu/-apple/-cpu`; the older `-ane` spelling of the Apple tier stays accepted). This is the **early artifact gate**: if the requested model folds onto the `expression-2` / `essence-2` families and the agent's trained per-identity model hasn't been generated yet, the request is rejected `409 MODEL_NOT_GENERATED` instead of failing later at session dispatch. Unknown values return `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` listing the accepted names. Omitted → the agent's own default model.

parameters.name: agent_id
parameters.description: Agent code (e.g. A23WJF0199)

parameters.name: fingerprint
parameters.description: Stable per-device hex string used for session tracking and per-visitor rate limiting. Required.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Optional. Request a specific avatar model for the embed session — a model name (`essence-1`, `expression-1`, `essence-2`, `expression-2`) or a force-tier slug that pins one serving tier (`expression-2-gpu/-cpu/-apple`, `essence-2-gpu/-apple/-cpu`; the older `-ane` spelling of the Apple tier stays accepted). This is the **early artifact gate**: if the requested model folds onto the `expression-2` / `essence-2` families and the agent's trained per-identity model hasn't been generated yet, the request is rejected `409 MODEL_NOT_GENERATED` instead of failing later at session dispatch. Unknown values return `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` listing the accepted names. Omitted → the agent's own default model.

tool_signatures.name: requestRuntimeToken
tool_signatures.description:
Exchange your API secret for a short-lived runtime token that authorizes one avatar session. The SDKs call this for you; call it directly when building a custom runtime. Free to call; the session it authorizes is billed per `GET /v1/pricing`.

**With `mode`, the same endpoint starts a cloud avatar** in your LiveKit room instead: send `mode`, `agent_id` (or `image` for an Expression 1 photo), `livekit_url`, `livekit_token` and `room_name`. The avatar joins as `bithuman-avatar-agent` and lip-syncs the audio you stream to it. The token, audio and latency rules are on [Cloud avatar without the plugin](https://docs.bithuman.ai/platforms/livekit/cloud-avatar).

**`fingerprint` must be at least 32 characters** when you send it. A shorter one is rejected `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` — a common surprise when a custom runtime passes a short device id. It is optional: leave it out rather than send a short one.

tool_signatures.name: revealApiSecret
tool_signatures.description:
Console-only: only the signed-in owner can reveal a stored secret, in
the console under Developer → API Secrets. Called with an API secret
it always returns `403 SECRET_REVEAL_CONSOLE_ONLY`, so one leaked
secret cannot read your others.

tool_signatures.name: revokeAllRuntimeKeys
tool_signatures.description:
The emergency stop: disables **every** runtime key on the account. Live
sessions stop within one refresh cycle (about 5 minutes). It does not
delete your API secrets; creating a new API secret clears the
suspension.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Free-text reason.

tool_signatures.name: terminateRuntimeSession
tool_signatures.description:
Stops **one** session; never touches an API secret. The session stops
counting toward your plan's concurrent sessions at once.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Free-text stop reason.

tool_signatures.name: testWebhook
tool_signatures.description: Deliver a one-off `ping` event to verify the endpoint is reachable.

tool_signatures.name: updateAgent
tool_signatures.description:
Update an existing agent's system prompt, its provider selection, or
both. The agent must already exist (use `POST /v1/agent/generate` to
create one). Send at least one of `system_prompt` and `providers` — a
body with neither is rejected `400 MISSING_PARAM`.

**An agent's `name` cannot be set here, and cannot be set at
creation either.** Names are generated from the agent's prompt and
portrait. A body whose only field is `name` changes nothing and
returns `400 MISSING_PARAM`; sending `name` alongside `system_prompt`
updates the prompt and ignores the name.

system_prompt.description: New system prompt for the agent.
system_prompt.example: You are a professional sales assistant.

providers.description: Which provider each capability uses for this agent. Give a capability `"default"` to use the platform's own provider, or an object `{"mode": "custom", "provider_id": "<id>"}` to point it at one you registered yourself. The patch is merged, so a capability you omit keeps its current selection. An unknown capability name, an unusable selection, or a `provider_id` that is not registered on your account is refused `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` at write time with the reason — nothing is stored half-configured.

parameters.name: providers
parameters.description: Which provider each capability uses for this agent. Give a capability `"default"` to use the platform's own provider, or an object `{"mode": "custom", "provider_id": "<id>"}` to point it at one you registered yourself. The patch is merged, so a capability you omit keeps its current selection. An unknown capability name, an unusable selection, or a `provider_id` that is not registered on your account is refused `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` at write time with the reason — nothing is stored half-configured.

parameters.name: system_prompt
parameters.description: New system prompt for the agent.

tool_signatures.name: updateDynamics
tool_signatures.description:
Update gesture settings for an agent. After a successful update,
movements regeneration is automatically triggered in the background.

`result` (model path/hash when generated), `talking` (default model path/hash).

talking.description: Default talking model path and hash (used when dynamics are disabled).

toggle_enabled.description: `true` to switch agent to dynamics model, `false` to restore default talking model.

parameters.name: dynamics
parameters.description:
Dynamics configuration to merge with existing data.
Fields: `enabled` (boolean), `batch_results` (gesture results),
`result` (model path/hash when generated), `talking` (default model path/hash).

enabled.description: Enable or disable dynamics for this agent.

batch_results.description: Map of gesture names to video generation results.

parameters.description: `true` to switch agent to dynamics model, `false` to restore default talking model.

tool_signatures.name: updateProviders
tool_signatures.description:
Replaces your provider list: `entries` is the **whole** list, and
`{"entries": []}` clears every provider. Existing entries are matched by
`id` and merged (unspecified credentials are kept); new entries get a
generated id. Returns the same masked shape as `GET`.

id.description: Existing entry id to update; omit to add a new one.

label.description: Display name; defaults to the platform name.

credentials.description: Key/value credentials. Sensitive keys are encrypted at rest.

tool_signatures.name: uploadFile
tool_signatures.description:
Upload images, videos, audio, or documents — by public URL or as
base64. Files are organized by type, and the type is read from the
file's own bytes: `file_type` and the filename extension are both
cross-checked against them, never trusted over them. The response
returns a public URL for the stored file.

tool_signatures.name: validateApiSecret
tool_signatures.description:
Verify that your API secret is valid and your account is active.

Always returns HTTP 200. Inspect the `valid` field in the body
to determine outcome — invalid or missing credentials yield
`{"valid": false}` rather than a 401. The secret goes in the
`api-secret` header; a secret sent as `Authorization: Bearer` is
not read and also yields `{"valid": false}`.

tool_signatures.name: validateSelfHostedKey
tool_signatures.description:
The bitHuman SDKs, the CLI and the plugins call this for you when a
self-hosted session starts and while it runs; you call it only if you
build your own runtime. Deleting a key in the dashboard stops a running
self-hosted session at its next check.

A runtime treats the three answers differently:

| status | meaning | what a runtime should do |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | valid | serve |
| `401` | **definite**: unknown, revoked or disabled | stop |
| `503` | we cannot tell right now | retry, keep serving |

A `503` is never a statement about your key: keep serving and retry.

billing_type.description:
The self-hosted product this runtime serves. Always send
the key for the product you run.

parameters.name: billing_type
parameters.description:
The self-hosted product this runtime serves. Always send
the key for the product you run.
